manifesto.title: Manifesto
manifesto.citation.text: An organism feeds on negative entropy.
manifesto.chapter.1.1: Order is structure, logic, and the interconnection of elements
manifesto.chapter.1.2: . Entropy is randomness, chaos, and unpredictability. Life creates order out of chaos, while death returns everything to a state of maximum entropy.
manifesto.chapter.2.1: An organism, as an ordered system, does not exist in isolation — it is made up of simpler parts, it is part of something more complex, and it constantly interacts with its environment. Development and evolution are the pursuit of greater efficiency and a path toward higher levels of order.
manifesto.chapter.3.1: My moral intuition is rooted in a simple principle:
manifesto.chapter.3.2: good is that which increases order
manifesto.chapter.3.3: ; bad is that which leads to destruction, uncertainty, and chaos. I see this principle as universal. It applies to everyday life: to thinking, to ethics, and consequently, to my professional activity.
manifesto.chapter.4.1: A good product makes the world better
manifesto.chapter.4.2: : it solves people’s problems and makes life easier, more beautiful, safer, or more interesting. It has meaning and intention, and its impact on the environment is positive. If a product survives by deceiving, imitating, manipulating, or exploiting human weaknesses — it is a bad product.
manifesto.chapter.5.2: between user and system. It is productive and goal-oriented. It feels pleasant, speaks in a polite tone, and looks aesthetically clean. It fits the context — situational, cultural, and temporal. It is honest, clearly communicates what matters, and avoids dark patterns. It is concise, with no unnecessary noise or distractions.
manifesto.chapter.6.1: Good code is logically structured, easy to read, maintain, and extend
manifesto.chapter.6.2: . At the same time, it should be optimized — because the ability to solve problems with minimal energy is a trait of the most adaptive systems.
manifesto.chapter.7.1: I see my role as bringing order into environments
manifesto.chapter.7.2: and resisting entropy through my work — through code, interfaces, and software products
manifesto.chapter.7.3: To solve problems and make decisions,
manifesto.chapter.7.4: I look for the essence of things
manifesto.chapter.7.5: and rely on more fundamental principles to find the right answer.
manifesto.chapter.7.7: , because every complex system is made up of small parts working together.
manifesto.chapter.7.8: I consider all systems in context
manifesto.chapter.7.9: , taking into account their structure and environment, to achieve efficient interaction and harmony.
